scheme_name: Financial Assistance To Disabled Students Pursuing (10th, 11th, 12th Equivalent Exams)
description:
The Financial Assistance to Disabled Students Pursuing 10th, 11th, and 12th Equivalent Exams scheme is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at supporting students with disabilities.

This scheme was launched in 2009 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to students with disabilities who are pursuing their education at the secondary and higher secondary levels.

The scheme aims to promote educational opportunities for disabled students and to reduce the financial burden on their families.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is intended to cover various educational expenses such as tuition fees, books, and other necessary materials.

The exact amount of financial assistance provided to eligible students is ₹3,000 per annum for students in classes 10 to 12.

This assistance is aimed at students who are enrolled in recognized schools or educational institutions.

The scheme targets students with disabilities who have a disability certificate issued by a competent authority.

To be eligible for this scheme, students must be between the ages of 14 and 18 years.

The disability must be at least 40 percent as certified by a medical authority.

Students must be pursuing their education in recognized schools or institutions that are affiliated with the respective state boards or central boards.

The application process for this scheme involves several steps.

Eligible students must obtain an application form from the local office of the Department of Social Welfare or download it from the official government website.

The completed application form must be submitted along with necessary documents such as the disability certificate, proof of age, and proof of enrollment in school.

Students must also provide their bank account details for direct transfer of the financial assistance.

The application must be submitted to the respective state government or union territory administration.

The application is usually processed within a period of three to six months.

Once approved, the financial assistance is disbursed directly into the bank accounts of the beneficiaries.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment through its various state and union territory departments.

Each state has its own designated office to handle the applications and disbursement of funds.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to enhance the educational opportunities for persons with disabilities in India.

According to the 2011 Census, there are approximately 2.68 crore persons with disabilities in India.

Of these, a significant number are children and adolescents who require support for their education.

The government aims to ensure that disabled students have equal access to education and can pursue their academic goals.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is a crucial step towards achieving this goal.

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also aims to create awareness about the rights of disabled students.

The government encourages schools to adopt inclusive practices that support the learning needs of disabled students.

The scheme is reviewed periodically to assess its effectiveness and to make necessary adjustments.

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account to improve the implementation of the scheme.

The government also collaborates with non-governmental organizations to reach out to potential beneficiaries.

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform disabled students and their families about the availability of this financial assistance.

The scheme aligns with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016, which emphasizes the right to education for all.

The government aims to increase the enrollment of disabled students in secondary and higher secondary education through this initiative.

The financial assistance is provided on an annual basis and is subject to renewal each year.

Students must reapply for the assistance each academic year to continue receiving support.

The scheme also encourages students to complete their education and pursue higher studies.

The government has set a target to increase the literacy rate among disabled individuals through such initiatives.

The implementation of this scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare policies aimed at empowering persons with disabilities.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment conducts regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme.

Reports on the number of beneficiaries and the amount disbursed are published annually.

The scheme has seen a steady increase in the number of beneficiaries since its inception.

In 2020-2021, approximately 50,000 students benefited from this financial assistance.

The government has allocated a budget of ₹150 crore for the scheme in the financial year 2021-2022.

This allocation is expected to cater to the increasing number of applications received each year.

The scheme is an important part of the government's commitment to social justice and inclusion.

It reflects the government's recognition of the challenges faced by disabled students in accessing education.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is a vital resource for many families.

It helps alleviate the financial strain associated with educational expenses.

The scheme is a significant step towards creating an equitable education system in India.

The government continues to explore ways to enhance the support provided to disabled students.

This includes reviewing the financial assistance amount and expanding eligibility criteria.

The scheme is a testament to the government's ongoing efforts to promote inclusivity in education.

The financial assistance to disabled students pursuing 10th, 11th, and 12th equivalent exams is a crucial initiative that aims to empower students with disabilities.

By providing financial support, the government seeks to ensure that these students can pursue their education without financial hindrance.

This initiative is a part of India's commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals related to education and equality.
